items.text: In family caregivers of people with dementia attending memory clinics or similar specialist services, does routine burden screening followed by referral or support, compared with usual care, reduce caregiver burden, depression or poor quality of life, or delay care home admission of the person with dementia?
items.population: Family caregivers of people with dementia in specialist services
items.intervention: Routine burden screening followed by referral or support
items.outcome: Caregiver burden at about 12 months; depression; quality of life; care home admission
items.setting: Memory clinics and similar specialist dementia services

finer: Feasible for two reviewers with library support; interesting and relevant to the clinic's decision; novel in separating screening from support; ethical as a review.
